# Real opportunity sourcing and requirement extraction

## Scope and timing

Before any external search, the participant must explicitly provide a CV (or
adequate CV text), career direction, geographical/remote preference, and target
level (including `unsure`). Ask for missing items together, then wait. Do not
guess from historical profile data or examples. Search ads/calls yourself when
browsing is available: the participant need not provide them.

Default to **employment vacancies**. Search or compare research funding,
fellowships, scholarships and other programmes **only if explicitly named in the
participant's goal**. If several types are explicitly named, preserve distinct
opportunity types and separate source/eligibility checks; a single coherent
roadmap may still address shared priorities. Aim for 3–5 included opportunities
**overall**, not per type. A single readable authentic source is enough for a
labelled single-source assessment.

## Source record: preserve these fields

| Field | Check |
|---|---|
| Identity | Actual title, opportunity type, employer/funder/provider |
| Geography | Work location or intended host region; remote/mobility/residence requirements where relevant |
| Access | Actual original URL, readable source or participant-supplied full text |
| Time | Date checked; verified-open/closed/historical/not-verified status; stated deadline |
| Level | Advertised employment seniority OR programme applicant category (not interchangeable) |
| Criterion | Quote briefly or precisely paraphrase attributable source text |
| Status of criterion | `REQUIRED`, `EXPECTED/PREFERRED`, `JOB TASK`, `ADVANTAGE`, `SELECTION CRITERION`, `UNCLEAR` |

A Google result snippet, inaccessible page or undated programme homepage is NOT
proof of current availability. A provider's enduring programme description is
not confirmation that the present year's call is open. If the source is
inaccessible, request readable text instead of fabricating conditions. A
participant-supplied old call is historical unless actually reverified.

## Selection criteria are NOT automatic disqualifiers

`REQUIRED` indicates a source-stated mandatory condition; a directly
contradicted candidate fact can produce `ELIGIBILITY_BARRIER` for that named
opportunity. Do not apply this label solely on absence of a degree, qualification,
letter, licence or years from a CV. `SELECTION CRITERION` indicates a competitive
assessment factor: potentially valuable for preparation, but NOT automatically
an eligibility rule. Similarly distinguish tasks, preferences and advantages.

Funding calls may specify applicant/PI status, host letters, geographical mobility,
residence windows, award categories, eligible institutional arrangements, and
selection standards. Research these **only where actually present in readable
call text**. Do not use a candidate's entry-level self-label as evidence of
eligibility for an academic funding scheme.

## R-ID design

Derive roughly 8–12 distinct meaningful requirements (R01 onward) or fewer when
sources justify. Attach each to actual source, opportunity type and track.
Cross-source merging is permitted only for substantively equivalent competencies.
Keep contradictory funding eligibility, local licensing, explicit language
mandates, career levels or specialist responsibilities in distinct rows. Never
construct a fictional average job/call or unsupported labour-market frequencies.

## No-browsing fallback

Ask for one genuine posting/call or full source text, then STOP. Do not invent
company/funder evidence, opening status, deadlines, odds, requirements or salary.
